# RFC-0001: aoska backend consumption of omactl package operations

> **Version:** 0.1.1 | **Status:** draft | **Phase:** spec

---

## 1. Summary

### [RFC-0001:C-SUMMARY] Summary (Informative) <a id="rfc-0001c-summary"></a>

This RFC specifies how the aoska backend consumes package-management capabilities through the omactl CLI/JSON contract.

**Scope:** This RFC covers aoska backend dependency boundaries, command invocation, capability checks, JSON parsing, error handling, update planning, package operation execution, unit state presentation, and static-catalog separation.

**Out of scope:** This RFC does not define the omactl producer API, visual UI layout, static software catalog metadata, or concrete frontend component structure. The omactl producer contract is tracked in the omactl repository as `docs/rfc/RFC-0001.md` at `https://github.com/AOSC-Dev/omactl`; this repository-local RFC owns aoska's consumer obligations.

**Rationale:** aoska should be a GUI and orchestration layer over omactl rather than a second package-manager frontend linked directly to oma internals.

---

## 2. Specification

### [RFC-0001:C-CLI-ONLY-INTEGRATION] CLI-only Package Integration (Normative) <a id="rfc-0001c-cli-only-integration"></a>

aoska backend package-management code MUST NOT link directly against `oma-pm`, `oma-utils`, `oma-fetch`, `oma-tum`, `oma-apt`, or other oma internal Rust crates for package state, planning, TUM classification, or package-changing operations.

aoska backend package-management code MUST obtain package-management state, operation plans, operation starts, unit status, unit results, and unit logs through omactl commands that satisfy the external omactl CLI/JSON contract.

aoska MAY keep dependencies needed for Tauri, static catalog fetching, JSON decoding, UI-owned metadata, and non-package-manager functionality.

**Rationale:** This removes the crate-version skew between aoska and the system-installed oma binary and keeps package-manager internals outside the GUI process.

### [RFC-0001:C-CAPABILITY-CHECKS] Capability Checks (Normative) <a id="rfc-0001c-capability-checks"></a>

aoska MUST run `omactl capabilities --json` before enabling a package-management flow that depends on omactl.

aoska MUST require the capabilities response to be a successful omactl JSON envelope with `schema_version` equal to `1`, `ok` equal to `true`, `kind` equal to `omactl.capabilities`, and `data.capabilities` as an array of strings.

aoska MUST require `query.upgradable.v1` before enabling the update-list flow.

aoska MUST require `query.installed.v1` before enabling installed inventory, update/uninstall rows, or selected remove flows derived from package-manager state.

aoska MUST require `query.package-detail.v1` before enabling package-detail data that is derived from APT or oma state.

aoska MUST require `plan.upgrade.v1`, `plan.install.v1`, and `plan.remove.v1` before enabling all-upgrade, install, or remove preview flows respectively.

aoska MUST require `plan.upgrade.selected.v1` before enabling selected-upgrade preview flows that pass a non-empty package list to `omactl plan upgrade --json <package>...`.

aoska MUST require `run.upgrade.v1`, `run.install.v1`, and `run.remove.v1` before enabling all-upgrade, install, or remove execution flows respectively.

aoska MUST require `run.upgrade.selected.v1` before enabling selected-upgrade execution flows that pass a non-empty package list to `omactl run upgrade --json <package>...`.

aoska MUST require `run.refresh.v1` before enabling package metadata refresh or check-update flows that schedule omactl work.

aoska MUST require `unit.cancel.v1` before enabling operation cancellation controls.

aoska MUST require `unit.status.v1`, `unit.result.v1`, and `unit.logs.v1` before presenting scheduled operation progress, terminal results, or operation logs respectively.

aoska MAY enable live package search only when `query.search.v1` is present.

aoska MAY enable package-manager-derived storage summaries only when `query.storage.v1` or an equivalent future storage capability is present.

aoska MUST enable TUM/security grouping only when `plan.tum.v1` is present and the relevant plan response reports that TUM data is available.

aoska MUST treat a missing capability required by the current flow as an integration error.

aoska SHOULD present a user-facing diagnostic when omactl or oma is too old for the requested package-management flow.

aoska SHOULD include the missing capability identifier in developer-facing diagnostics.

**Rationale:** The migration moves failures from compile-time crate availability to runtime CLI capability availability, so aoska needs explicit capability gates.

### [RFC-0001:C-JSON-CONSUMPTION] JSON Consumption (Normative) <a id="rfc-0001c-json-consumption"></a>

aoska MUST parse omactl's aoska-facing JSON envelope for package-management operations.

aoska MUST require `schema_version`, `ok`, and `kind` in aoska-facing JSON responses.

aoska MUST reject package-management JSON documents whose `schema_version` is not `1` unless a future aoska RFC explicitly permits that schema version.

aoska MUST dispatch successful payload parsing by the `kind` value returned by omactl.

aoska MUST treat `ok: false` responses as structured errors rather than successful payloads.

aoska MUST ignore unknown JSON fields in successful and failed omactl envelopes.

aoska MUST NOT parse human-readable oma, omactl, systemctl, or journalctl output for package-management state or operation status.

aoska SHOULD preserve the original omactl `kind` value in developer-facing diagnostics when payload parsing fails.

**Rationale:** A single JSON parse path keeps the backend robust against localization, color output, pager output, and terminal formatting changes while allowing omactl to add fields compatibly.

### [RFC-0001:C-TAURI-COMMAND-SURFACE] Tauri Package Manager Command Surface (Normative) <a id="rfc-0001c-tauri-command-surface"></a>

aoska MUST expose frontend package-management use cases through Tauri commands whose names start with `pm_`.

aoska MUST provide a capability command named `pm_capabilities` that wraps `omactl capabilities --json` and gates package-management features before they are enabled in the frontend.

aoska MUST provide query commands for update summary, update list, installed inventory, and package runtime state under the package-manager command surface, including `pm_update_summary`, `pm_list_updates`, `pm_list_installed`, and `pm_package_state` or future commands that explicitly supersede them.

aoska MUST provide planning commands for update, install, and remove previews under the package-manager command surface, including `pm_plan_update`, `pm_plan_install`, and `pm_plan_remove` or future commands that explicitly supersede them.

aoska MUST provide operation-start commands for update, install, remove, and refresh/check flows under the package-manager command surface, including `pm_start_update`, `pm_start_install`, `pm_start_remove`, and `pm_start_refresh` or future commands that explicitly supersede them.

aoska MUST provide operation observation commands under the package-manager command surface, including `pm_operation_status`, `pm_operation_result`, `pm_operation_logs`, `pm_follow_operation_logs`, and `pm_cancel_operation` or future commands that explicitly supersede them.

aoska MAY provide `pm_storage_summary` to expose storage presentation data that combines omactl runtime size primitives with aoska catalog membership.

aoska MUST NOT expose raw oma crate-shaped types as the long-term frontend package-management API.

**Rationale:** The frontend should depend on app-store use cases and omactl JSON semantics, not on historical Rust crate shapes or raw command-line details.

### [RFC-0001:C-UPDATE-FLOWS] Update Query and Planning Flows (Normative) <a id="rfc-0001c-update-flows"></a>

aoska MUST obtain the update-list package set by invoking `omactl query upgradable --json` or a future capability that explicitly supersedes `query.upgradable.v1`.

aoska MUST compute update counts from omactl query or plan responses rather than from direct oma crates.

aoska MUST obtain all-upgrade preview details by invoking `omactl plan upgrade --json` before presenting a machine-derived all-upgrade plan.

aoska MUST obtain selected-upgrade preview details by invoking `omactl plan upgrade --json <package>...` before presenting a machine-derived selected-upgrade plan, and MUST gate that flow on `plan.upgrade.selected.v1`.

aoska MUST preserve the selected package list as structured process arguments rather than as a shell fragment.

aoska MUST obtain install preview details by invoking `omactl plan install --json <package>...` before presenting a machine-derived install plan.

aoska MUST obtain remove preview details by invoking `omactl plan remove --json <package>...` before presenting a machine-derived remove plan.

aoska MUST obtain package details derived from APT or oma state by invoking `omactl query package-detail --json <package>...`.

aoska MUST obtain TUM and security-update grouping from omactl plan responses when `plan.tum.v1` is advertised and the plan response reports TUM data as available.

aoska MUST distinguish unavailable TUM data from an empty security-update set.

aoska MUST NOT present security-update counts as known when `plan.tum.v1` is absent or when the relevant plan response reports TUM data as unavailable.

aoska MAY present a user-facing "security classification unavailable" state when TUM data is unavailable.

**Rationale:** The update UI currently depends on oma crate-derived data. This clause defines the required replacement behavior for the CLI-contract migration and prevents aoska from confusing unknown security classification with zero security updates.

### [RFC-0001:C-INSTALLED-INVENTORY-SELECTION] Installed Inventory and Selected Actions (Normative) <a id="rfc-0001c-installed-inventory-selection"></a>

aoska MUST obtain installed package inventory for the update/uninstall surface by invoking `omactl query installed --json` through the package-manager backend layer or a future capability that explicitly supersedes `query.installed.v1`.

aoska MUST require `query.installed.v1` before enabling installed-list rows that are derived from package-manager state.

aoska MUST join installed inventory with static catalog metadata by stable package references rather than by localized display names.

aoska MUST preserve an omactl-provided package key such as `name_without_arch` or an equivalent stable package identifier when matching installed, upgradable, and catalog entries.

aoska MUST distinguish aoska-catalog-manageable software, other oma-managed software, non-oma-managed storage, and free space when those categories are presented.

aoska MUST obtain selected update preview data by invoking `omactl plan upgrade --json <package>...` when a non-empty selected update set is previewed, and MUST gate that action on `plan.upgrade.selected.v1`.

aoska MUST start selected update execution by invoking `omactl run upgrade --json <package>...` when a non-empty selected update set is executed, and MUST gate that action on `run.upgrade.selected.v1`.

aoska MUST treat an empty selected update set as an invalid frontend action unless the user explicitly chose an all-updates flow.

aoska MUST obtain selected remove preview data by invoking `omactl plan remove --json <package>...` before presenting machine-derived remove consequences for selected installed packages.

aoska MUST start selected remove execution by invoking `omactl run remove --json <package>...` for selected removable packages.

aoska MUST disable selected update and selected remove actions until at least one eligible package is selected.

aoska MUST NOT infer remove eligibility solely from static catalog membership.

**Rationale:** Issue #33 requires installed/update/uninstall rows and selected batch actions while preserving omactl as the runtime truth for package state and operation eligibility.

### [RFC-0001:C-REFRESH-CANCEL-FLOWS] Refresh, Check, and Cancel Flows (Normative) <a id="rfc-0001c-refresh-cancel-flows"></a>

aoska MUST obtain update-check or metadata-refresh scheduling through `omactl run refresh --json` or a future capability that explicitly supersedes `run.refresh.v1`.

aoska MUST require `run.refresh.v1` before enabling a refresh/check action that schedules package-manager work.

aoska MUST treat a successful refresh/check start response as scheduling success, not as refresh completion.

aoska MUST retain the returned refresh/check unit identifier until the terminal result has been read or the operation has been cancelled and surfaced.

aoska MUST use `omactl status --json <unit>` and `omactl result --json <unit>` to present refresh/check progress and terminal state.

aoska MUST obtain refresh/check logs through omactl log commands rather than by invoking `journalctl` directly.

aoska MUST cancel package-manager operations by invoking `omactl cancel --json <unit>` or a future capability that explicitly supersedes `unit.cancel.v1`.

aoska MUST require `unit.cancel.v1` before enabling cancel controls for refresh, install, update, or remove operations.

aoska MUST distinguish user-cancelled operations from failed operations when omactl exposes a cancelled terminal state.

aoska SHOULD refresh package state after refresh/check, install, update, remove, or cancel flows reach a terminal state.

**Rationale:** The GUI needs checking, progress, cancellation, and recovery states without owning systemd or package-manager lifetime semantics directly.

### [RFC-0001:C-OPERATION-FLOWS] Package Operation Flows (Normative) <a id="rfc-0001c-operation-flows"></a>

aoska MUST start package-changing all-upgrade operations by invoking `omactl run upgrade --json` or a future capability that explicitly supersedes `run.upgrade.v1`.

aoska MUST start package-changing selected-upgrade operations by invoking `omactl run upgrade --json <package>...` only when `run.upgrade.selected.v1` is present, or when a future capability explicitly supersedes selected upgrade execution semantics.

aoska MUST start package-changing install operations by invoking `omactl run install --json <package>...` or a future capability that explicitly supersedes `run.install.v1`.

aoska MUST start package-changing remove operations by invoking `omactl run remove --json <package>...` or a future capability that explicitly supersedes `run.remove.v1`.

aoska MUST pass package names, operation flags, and unit identifiers to omactl as structured process arguments.

aoska MUST pass package paths to omactl only when the invoked omactl operation explicitly accepts local package paths.

aoska MUST NOT build shell fragments from package names, package paths, operation flags, or unit identifiers.

aoska MUST treat a successful `omactl run` response as scheduling success, not as package-operation success.

aoska MUST retain the returned `data.unit` value for each scheduled package-changing operation until the terminal state has been recorded and either surfaced to the frontend or persisted in backend history.

aoska MAY forget a completed operation after its terminal state and final diagnostics have been surfaced or persisted.

aoska MUST use `omactl status --json <unit>` to obtain operation state for a retained unit.

aoska MUST use `omactl result --json <unit>` to obtain terminal result information for a retained unit.

aoska MUST use `omactl logs --json <unit>` or `omactl logs --json --follow <unit>` to obtain operation logs for a retained unit.

aoska MUST distinguish scheduling failure from unit execution failure after scheduling.

aoska MUST use `omactl cancel --json <unit>` to request cancellation for an omactl-managed operation when cancellation is enabled.

**Rationale:** aoska needs systemd-backed package operation lifetime management while keeping shell and privilege boundaries outside the GUI process.

### [RFC-0001:C-OPERATION-EVENTS-LOGS] Operation Events and Logs (Normative) <a id="rfc-0001c-operation-events-logs"></a>

aoska MUST obtain accumulated operation logs by invoking `omactl logs --json <unit>` through the package-manager backend layer.

aoska MUST obtain live operation log streams by invoking `omactl logs --json --follow <unit>` through the package-manager backend layer when live logs are presented.

aoska MUST consume live omactl log output as JSON Lines where each line is one complete JSON event envelope.

aoska MUST validate each JSON Lines event before emitting it to the frontend as a structured package-manager event.

aoska MUST NOT invoke `journalctl` directly for package-manager operation logs, progress, status, or event streaming.

aoska MUST NOT parse human-readable `journalctl`, `systemctl`, `oma`, or omactl text output to derive package operation events.

aoska MUST preserve the operation unit identifier on emitted frontend events so consumers can correlate events with the operation that produced them.

aoska SHOULD tolerate unknown fields in operation log/event envelopes.

aoska SHOULD surface malformed omactl event output as an integration error without treating the package operation itself as successful.

**Rationale:** omactl owns the journal/systemd boundary; aoska owns typed frontend events derived from omactl JSON and JSON Lines.

### [RFC-0001:C-STORAGE-SUMMARY] Storage Summary (Normative) <a id="rfc-0001c-storage-summary"></a>

aoska MAY expose a storage summary through `pm_storage_summary` when omactl provides storage or installed-size primitives.

aoska MUST obtain package-manager-derived storage primitives through `omactl query storage --json`, installed inventory payloads, or future omactl JSON capabilities that explicitly supersede them.

aoska MUST join omactl runtime size data with aoska catalog membership to compute app-store presentation groups such as aoska-manageable software, other oma-managed software, non-oma-managed space, and free space.

aoska MUST NOT treat static catalog metadata as authoritative for installed size, disk free space, package ownership, or package-manager-managed storage.

aoska MUST label estimated or unavailable storage values distinctly from exact values when omactl marks them as estimated or unavailable.

aoska MUST keep storage summary failure separate from install, update, remove, and refresh operation failure.

aoska MAY hide storage summary details when required omactl storage capabilities are absent.

**Rationale:** The update/uninstall design needs storage presentation, but only omactl can provide runtime package and disk facts while aoska can provide catalog grouping.

### [RFC-0001:C-COMPATIBILITY-WRAPPERS] Compatibility Wrapper Deprecation (Normative) <a id="rfc-0001c-compatibility-wrappers"></a>

aoska MAY keep compatibility Tauri commands with historical names during frontend migration.

aoska MUST implement any retained `fetch_update_count`, `fetch_update_detail`, `fetch_update_all`, `fetch_update_tum`, `fetch_tum_update`, or other `fetch_update_*` package-manager compatibility wrapper by delegating to the new package-manager backend layer that consumes omactl JSON.

aoska MUST implement any retained `oma_*` package-manager compatibility wrapper by delegating to the new package-manager backend layer that consumes omactl JSON.

aoska MUST NOT keep compatibility wrappers that directly call oma internal Rust crates, parse human-oriented command output, or invoke `journalctl` directly.

aoska MUST mark compatibility wrappers as deprecated in code comments or generated API documentation when they remain after the package-manager backend layer is introduced.

aoska MUST remove compatibility wrappers after frontend callers migrate to the `pm_*` command surface, unless a later RFC explicitly extends their lifetime.

aoska SHOULD keep compatibility wrapper response shapes as small adapters over the canonical `pm_*` responses rather than as independent business logic.

**Rationale:** Temporary wrappers reduce migration risk, but the old command names must not preserve the old integration boundary or become a second package-manager API.

### [RFC-0001:C-ERROR-HANDLING] Error Handling (Normative) <a id="rfc-0001c-error-handling"></a>

aoska MUST map omactl structured error codes to backend error states.

aoska MUST preserve the original omactl error code in developer-facing diagnostics when an omactl error envelope contains a code.

aoska MUST distinguish scheduling failure from package-operation failure after scheduling.

aoska MUST distinguish `INVALID_ARGUMENTS`, `UNSUPPORTED_COMMAND`, `OMA_BUSY`, `AUTHORIZATION_FAILED`, `SYSTEMD_FAILED`, `OMA_EXEC_FAILED`, `TUM_UNAVAILABLE`, `UNKNOWN_UNIT`, `MALFORMED_DELEGATE_OUTPUT`, and `INTERNAL_ERROR` when omactl provides those codes.

aoska MUST treat an unrecognized omactl error code as a generic omactl integration error while preserving the original code for diagnostics.

aoska SHOULD map `OMA_BUSY` to a user-facing busy/package-manager-active state.

aoska SHOULD map `AUTHORIZATION_FAILED` to a user-facing permission or authentication failure state.

aoska SHOULD map `UNSUPPORTED_COMMAND` and missing capabilities to an upgrade-required diagnostic for omactl or oma.

aoska SHOULD map `TUM_UNAVAILABLE` to a security-classification-unavailable state instead of an empty security-update state.

**Rationale:** GUI state transitions need stable failure categories instead of inferred text patterns.

### [RFC-0001:C-STATIC-CATALOG] Static Catalog Boundary (Normative) <a id="rfc-0001c-static-catalog"></a>

aoska MAY continue to fetch and render static catalog indexes, recommendations, package detail metadata, screenshots, icons, and banners independently from omactl.

aoska MAY join static catalog metadata with package-management state obtained from omactl for presentation.

aoska MUST NOT use static catalog metadata as the source of installed state, upgradable state, operation plans, TUM/security classification, or package-changing operation status.

Package-management state derived from APT or oma MUST come from omactl.

**Rationale:** The omactl migration concerns package-management integration only. The app-store catalog remains a separate aoska product surface.
